comment: Known differences between two canonical graph dumps (jets/rulesbench/graphdump), read by rules_bench_diff and embedded in it. A difference is unclassified unless an entry matches. Fields and pair kinds: README.md beside this file. Each entry names where the difference is recorded: a section of jets/jetrules/rete/README.md or a register entry of projects/rules_benchmark. This built-in list holds only differences of the engines themselves. An entry that names a workload's predicates, rules, members or files is kept in that workload's own list, passed with -known (README.md).

entries.description: The line is the same on both sides up to the label of a minted node, under a one-to-one correspondence of labels: the node is on both sides and was renamed because its neighbourhood within three hops differs. What differs is in its own lines, which are classified on their own.

refs: jets/jetrules/rete/README.md, The Go and C++ engines are independently maintained and they disagree, item 3
entries.description: The Go engine quantises a double literal to 15 bits of mantissa (ResourceManager.NewDoubleLiteral); C++ keeps it. The two values are equal once both are quantised.

The Go engine names a lookup result jets:lookup:<key> (jets:lookup:multi:<key> for a multi-lookup), without the table, so two tables looked up with the same key share one subject, which carries both tables' columns and both rows' jets:row_id (LookupTableSqlite3.Lookup, jets/jetrules/rete/lookup_table_sqlite3.go). C++ names it jets:<table>:<key> (LookupTable::lookup_internal, jets/rete/lookup_sql_helper.cc), one subject per table. In the dump: one minted node on Go where C++ has one per table. Only a lookup subject: the merged node must be the object of a cache triple (jets:cache:<table> jets:lookup_row|jets:lookup_multi_rows _:node) on Go; any other node merged on one engine stays unclassified.
entries.subject: jets:cache:.*

entries.description: A multi-lookup's cache triple: Go writes (jets:cache:<table> jets:lookup_multi_rows <subject>) (LookupTableSqlite3.MultiLookup), C++ (<table> jets:lookup_row <subject>) (LookupTable::lookup_internal), which the dump renames jets:cache:<table>. Bookkeeping: the 26 uses of jets:lookup_row and jets:lookup_multi_rows in the four workspaces' rule files (counted 2026-10-20) all read them as (?x jets:lookup_… ?y), and none names a cache resource.
entries.subject: jets:cache:.*
